Administration structure CONFIRMED: like Hawaii's regular driver license program, CDL knowledge and skills testing in Hawaii is administered locally by the four County Commercial Driver Licensing Offices (City & County of Honolulu -- 897 2nd Street, Pearl City; County of Hawaii -- Hilo/West Hawaii/Waimea; County of Maui -- Maui/Molokai/Lanai; County of Kauai -- Lihue), each listed on the manual's own cover page as a 'COMMERCIAL DRIVER LICENSING OFFICE', rather than by a single centralized state DMV -- this was independently corroborated by the official honolulu.gov page 'Commercial Driver Licensing (CDL) Office | Department of Customer Services' (fetched 2026-08-21), which confirms the Honolulu CDL office is run by the City and County's own Department of Customer Services. All four counties use this one shared statewide AAMVA-based manual for CDL knowledge testing. Real exam mechanics: the 80% minimum passing score for the CDL general knowledge and endorsement knowledge tests is federally standardized under 49 CFR 383.135(a) and applies regardless of state. The manual itself (Section 1.1.1, Knowledge Tests) and the official honolulu.gov CDL office page both describe the general/special knowledge tests and their fee structure ($15 general knowledge test, $5 per special/endorsement knowledge test, $15 aural test surcharge) but neither states a specific total item count for the general knowledge test or any endorsement test -- only third-party test-prep sites (not hidot.hawaii.gov or any county .gov source) claim a '50 questions/40 correct' figure, so per this project's no-default-numeric-values discipline, no 'CDL Test Administration' item-count question was written for this track, consistent with the AL/AZ/AR/CO/DE hedging precedent. Content-depth rationale: this is the same substantial 2005 CDL Testing System AAMVA-authored manual used across most prior CDL-track states, covering Introduction/licensing (CDL classes A/B/C, six endorsements H/N/P/S/T/X, CLP rules, ELDT, medical certification, disqualifications), Driving Safely (vehicle control, stopping distance, space/speed management, hazardous conditions, railroad crossings, skids/emergencies, alcohol/drugs), Transporting Cargo Safely, Transporting Passengers Safely, Air Brakes, Combination Vehicles, Doubles and Triples, Tank Vehicles, Hazardous Materials (communication/placarding/loading plus driving rules/security/emergencies), School Buses, Vehicle Inspection, and Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test / On-Road Driving -- supporting a large, non-repetitive, well-grounded question pool. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
